# Nerdigy.Mediator LLM Reference

This file is optimized for machine ingestion. It summarizes package boundaries, key contracts, registration patterns, and runtime semantics for Nerdigy.Mediator 2.x.

## Package Boundaries

- `Nerdigy.Mediator.Contracts`
  - Public contracts and delegates only.
  - Use in shared libraries that define requests/notifications/handlers but do not host runtime dispatch.
- `Nerdigy.Mediator`
  - Core runtime dispatch for `Send`, `Publish`, and `CreateStream`.
  - Pipeline execution, exception processing, tracing and metrics.
  - `MediatorRegistry` for registering dispatch code ahead of time (Native AOT).
- `Nerdigy.Mediator.DependencyInjection`
  - DI registration: assembly scanning or explicit registration, with startup validation.
  - Includes runtime and contracts transitively.

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package Nerdigy.Mediator.DependencyInjection
```

## DI Registration

```csharp
using Nerdigy.Mediator.DependencyInjection;

services.AddMediator(options =>
{
    options.RegisterServicesFromAssemblyContaining<Program>();
});
```

This registers:
- `IMediator`
- `ISender`
- `IPublisher`
- scanned handlers, pipeline components, and exception components

Explicit registration (required for trimmed and Native AOT apps):

```csharp
services.AddMediator(options => options
    .AddRequestHandler<GetUserQuery, UserDto, GetUserQueryHandler>()
    .AddRequestHandler<DeleteUserCommand, DeleteUserCommandHandler>() // void request
    .AddStreamRequestHandler<GetOrdersStream, OrderDto, GetOrdersStreamHandler>()
    .AddNotificationHandler<UserCreated, SendWelcomeEmailHandler>()
    .AddBehavior<GetUserQuery, UserDto, CachingBehavior>()
    .AddOpenBehavior(typeof(LoggingBehavior<,>)));
```

Other `MediatorOptions` methods: `AddStreamBehavior`, `AddOpenStreamBehavior`, `AddPreProcessor`, `AddPostProcessor`,
`AddExceptionHandler`, `AddExceptionAction`, `AddStreamExceptionHandler`. Each takes an optional `ServiceLifetime`.
`AddMediator()` with no arguments registers only the mediator, for handlers registered directly in DI.

Registration rules (violations fail `AddMediator` with one `InvalidOperationException` listing every problem):
- Exactly one handler per request type. Two different handlers fail; an explicit handler replaces a scanned one; a handler registered in DI before `AddMediator` is kept.
- No component closed over an interface or abstract message type (e.g. `IPipelineBehavior<IAuditable, Unit>`, `INotificationHandler<INotification>`). Use an open generic constrained to the interface.
- No `IRequestHandler<TRequest, Unit>` for a request that implements `IRequest`; implement `IRequestHandler<TRequest>`.
- Scanned assemblies must load; set `options.IgnoreTypeLoadFailures = true` to scan what loaded.
- A singleton mediator cannot be combined with scoped components.
- A later `AddMediator` call cannot change `MediatorLifetime` or the publisher.
- Behaviors run explicit ones first in call order, then scanned ones in order of full type name.

Always resolve `IMediator` from a scope.

## Core Dispatch Contracts

```csharp
public interface IMediator : ISender, IPublisher;
```

```csharp
public interface ISender
{
    Task<TResponse> Send<TResponse>(IRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    Task Send(IRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    IAsyncEnumerable<TResponse> CreateStream<TResponse>(IStreamRequest<TResponse> request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

```csharp
public interface IPublisher
{
    Task Publish<TNotification>(TNotification notification, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        where TNotification : INotification;
}
```

## Message Contracts

```csharp
public interface IRequest<TResponse> : IBaseRequest;
public interface IRequest : IRequest<Unit>;
public interface IStreamRequest<TResponse> : IBaseRequest;
public interface INotification;
```

Rules:
- One request type maps to exactly one request handler.
- One stream request type maps to exactly one stream handler.
- Notifications can have zero to many handlers.

## Handler Contracts

```csharp
public interface IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>;
```

```csharp
public interface IRequestHandler<TRequest>
    where TRequest : IRequest;
```

```csharp
public interface IStreamRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>
    where TRequest : IStreamRequest<TResponse>;
```

```csharp
public interface INotificationHandler<TNotification>
    where TNotification : INotification;
```

## Pipeline Contracts

```csharp
public delegate Task<TResponse> RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse>(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
public delegate IAsyncEnumerable<TResponse> StreamHandlerDelegate<TResponse>(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
public interface IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest> where TRequest : IBaseRequest;
public interface IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>;
public interface IRequestPostProcessor<TRequest, TResponse> where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>;
public interface IStreamPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> where TRequest : IStreamRequest<TResponse>;
```

`next()` keeps the token the behavior received; `next(token)` passes a different token to inner behaviors and the handler.

Execution order for standard requests:
1. `IRequestPreProcessor<TRequest>` in registration order, outside every behavior
2. `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResponse>` outer to inner in registration order
3. handler
4. `IRequestPostProcessor<TRequest,TResponse>` in registration order, inside the innermost behavior

## Exception Contracts

```csharp
public interface IRequestExceptionHandler<TRequest, TResponse, TException>
    where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
    where TException : Exception;
```

```csharp
public interface IRequestExceptionAction<TRequest, TException>
    where TRequest : IBaseRequest
    where TException : Exception;
```

```csharp
public interface IStreamRequestExceptionHandler<TRequest, TResponse, TException>
    where TRequest : IStreamRequest<TResponse>
    where TException : Exception;
```

Semantics:
- Exception handlers run first, from most specific exception type to least specific.
- Calling `state.SetHandled(...)` suppresses rethrow and returns fallback response.
- Exception actions run only when no exception handler marked the exception handled. Every action runs, even when one fails.
- Each handler or action implementation runs once per exception, at the most specific level it matches.
- When the caller's token is canceled and the exception is `OperationCanceledException`, handlers are skipped; actions still run.
- If a handler, action, or failed-stream cleanup throws, `MediatorExceptionProcessingException` is thrown with the original as `InnerException` and the failures in `ProcessingExceptions`.
- Streams recover at most once per enumeration; the failed enumerator is disposed before the handler supplies a replacement.

## Notification Publisher Strategy

Options:
- `Sequential` (default): await each handler in order.
- `Parallel`: run handlers concurrently using `Task.WhenAll`.

Configure:

```csharp
options.UseNotificationPublishStrategy(NotificationPublishStrategy.Sequential);
```

or

```csharp
options.UseNotificationPublishStrategy(NotificationPublishStrategy.Parallel);
```

Parallel handlers share one scope. A custom publisher type is a singleton by default:
`options.UseNotificationPublisher<MyPublisher>(ServiceLifetime.Singleton)`.

## Native AOT

- Use explicit registration only; assembly scanning is `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`.
- Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection cannot close open generics over value types without dynamic code, including `Unit` for void requests. Under AOT, use `AddBehavior<TRequest, TResponse, TBehavior>()` for those requests.
- When constructing `Mediator` manually, call `MediatorRegistry.RegisterRequest<TRequest, TResponse>()`, `RegisterVoidRequest<TRequest>()`, `RegisterStreamRequest<TRequest, TResponse>()`, and `RegisterNotification<TNotification>()` at startup.

## Telemetry

- Activity source and meter: `MediatorTelemetry.ActivitySourceName` and `MediatorTelemetry.MeterName` (both `"Nerdigy.Mediator"`).
- Activities: `Nerdigy.Mediator.Send`, `Nerdigy.Mediator.Publish`, `Nerdigy.Mediator.Stream` (covers the whole enumeration).
- Instruments: `nerdigy.mediator.operation.duration` (s), `nerdigy.mediator.operation.active`, `nerdigy.mediator.publish.handlers`.
- Outcome tag `nerdigy.mediator.outcome`: `success`, `error`, `canceled`.
- No cost beyond a listener check when nothing listens. No `ILogger` in core.

## High-Signal Prompt Pattern

Use this when asking an LLM to generate code:

```text
Implement this feature using Nerdigy.Mediator 2.x on .NET 10.
Use IRequest/IRequestHandler for one-to-one request flows.
Use INotification/INotificationHandler for one-to-many fan-out.
Use IStreamRequest/IStreamRequestHandler for streaming.
Preserve cancellation tokens in all async paths; behaviors call next(cancellationToken).
Send requests with their declared response type (IRequest<T> is not covariant).
Register with services.AddMediator(options => options.RegisterServicesFromAssemblyContaining<...>()).
Output complete compileable files and minimal tests.
```
